notes: CONFORMS (2026-11-16, kb/Work PB5729 LANDED): the PARTIAL of the 1985 code reads was one defect, and it is fixed at its root. A REDEFINES subordinate to the second or later record of a multi-record FD overflowed the compiler's stack in StorageFormPass.Classify (alphanumeric data-name-2) or emitted C# naming a folded record (CS0103, numeric data-name-2). Cause: ClassifyRedefinesClassesPass.Run dissolves a class whose anchor lies under another class's redefining member, and tested the ancestor by the written clause text (RedefinesTargetName), so the implicit redefinition of a later record (RedefinesTarget set, no clause text) never dissolved the inner class: its anchor was both the canonical of its own class and a non-canonical view of the record-area class, and Classify forwarded it to itself. The ancestor test is now RedefinesTarget. Witnesses: conformance:cases/13.18.33-Level-number/pb5729_fd_later_record_redefines (2002, 2014, 2023) and, at 85, cases/VII.4.4@1985-READ-STATEMENT/pb5729_fd_later_record_redefines_85; with the fix reverted the first fails with CS0103. The prose that follows is the stored account of the rule, which holds. || kb/Work PB836 LANDED; kb/Work PB981 LANDED (determination D-FRA, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3). Sentence 1 - 'Multiple level 1 entries subordinate to a FD or SD entry represent implicit redefinitions of the same area': DataBinder.LinkImplicitRecordArea, the ONE linker for the FD and SD arms, joins every later CHARACTER-WINDOW level-1 record to the first through DataItem.SetRedefinition(first, RedefinitionKind.ImplicitFileRecord); the storage layout reads the one class for both constructs, while the 13.18.44.3 REDEFINES-clause screens read RedefinesKind == Clause only. Since PB981 a dynamic-length record, a variable-length group or a pointer-class record - legal source that used to be staged loud as COBOL0899 - is an OUT-OF-LINE record (FileModel.IsOutOfLineRecord): 8.5.1.10.3 lets its storage be located elsewhere, so it is never linked into the class and shares the area at the transfer boundary instead - a READ/RETURN makes the current record available in it (SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRecordAreaStore; a variable-length group through the one split rule CobolVarGroup.FromContiguous), and a WRITE/REWRITE/RELEASE sends its contiguous image (8.5.1.11.2). The 2014 golden writes and reads back a variable-length group, a dynamic-length record and a character record of one FD, a SAME RECORD AREA peer and an SD; the 2002 golden a pointer record beside a character record. Residue stated in D-FRA: an EXTERNAL file whose area has an out-of-line record, and a SORT/MERGE key that follows a variable-length member, are refused by name. Sentence 2 - report description level-1 entries are not implicit redefinitions: the report binder never calls SetRedefinition. EDITIONS 2002/2014/2023 as before; the FD rule is COBOL-85 base language and the same binder arm serves 85. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#ClassifyRedefinesClasses (the pass body moved from the DataBinder partial to its own IBindPass class under Binding/Passes (kb/Work PB2352, PB2353, PB2354)) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#LinkImplicitRecordArea (kb/Work PB2296 M7 moved the member from DataBinder to FileControlBinder (the file binder); the same rule is asked by the same code) EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED 2026-11-10: in force at 85, §1985:VI.5.7.4 GR3 'Multiple level 01 entries subordinate to any given level indicator other than the level indicator RD for a report description entry, represent implicit redefinitions of the same area' and §1985:XIII.3.14.4 GR2 'Multiple level 01 entries subordinate to a report description entry having the level indicator RD do not represent implicit redefinitions of the same area.'
